title: Final speed at impact
description: Essential: The student must correctly compute the ball's speed when it hits the ground, using energy conservation or kinematics from the break point.

title: Maximum rope tension
description: Essential: The student must calculate the maximum tension from the centripetal force at the lowest point before breaking.

title: Length for maximum range
description: Essential: The student must determine the optimal rope length l that maximizes the horizontal throw distance x.

title: Maximum horizontal distance
description: Essential: The student must compute the maximum possible horizontal distance x_max corresponding to the optimal length.

title: Projectile motion setup
description: Important: The student must correctly model the post-break motion as projectile motion with correct initial horizontal velocity and vertical drop.

title: Energy or kinematics application
description: Important: The student must apply work-energy theorem or appropriate kinematics to relate speeds at different points.

title: Optimization process
description: Important: The student must show a valid method (e.g., derivative, symmetry) to find the length that maximizes the range.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: All numerical answers should include correct SI units (m, m/s, N).

title: Sign or direction error
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the student uses incorrect signs for displacement or confuses vertical/horizontal components.

title: Centripetal force mistake
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the student omits the weight or uses incorrect net force (T - mg = mv^2/l) at the lowest point.
